payload.name: GPS-based Secret Key Establishment
payload.fact: Driving data from GPS receivers can be used to establish a 128-bit secret key between two legitimate devices co-located in a vehicle.
payload.boundary: The vehicle provides a physically secure boundary where devices co-located within the vehicle can observe common GPS data, while an attacker following the vehicle cannot.

provenance.title: DASK: Driving-Assisted Secret Key Establishment
provenance.quote_or_locus: Extensive experimental results show that when a user drives around 1.36 km for 1.32 minutes on average under moderate traffic conditions, two legitimate GPS-equipped devices in the vehicle can successfully establish a 128-bit secret key

provenance.title: DASK: Driving-Assisted Secret Key Establishment
provenance.quote_or_locus: A driving vehicle provides a physically secure boundary as the devices co-located within the vehicle can observe common GPS data, as opposed to devices that do not experience the trip
